page: Microsoft Azure F16-4amds_v7 is a constrained-vCPU virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, mapped directly to 4 vCPUs. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16) and cryptographic extensions like VAES and SHA-NI.

Despite its 4-vCPU allocation, the instance provides 128.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 32.0 GB per core ratio. This asymmetric configuration is coupled with a bundled 1888 GB NVMe SSD for fast local ephemeral storage, alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The server does not include dedicated GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In synthetic benchmarks, the 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC architecture delivers top-tier single-core stress-ng performance, placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Due to the limited 4-core count, multi-core stress-ng performance remains within the middle 50% tier. For specialized compute tasks, LLM text generation with small 135M parameter models reaches top-tier throughput at 357.27 tokens per second, though medium 7B model prompt processing drops to the bottom 25% bracket. Static web serving achieves average throughput at 10.66 GB/s.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, this constrained-core VM allows organizations running software with per-core licensing models to access high memory density and NVMe I/O capacity without paying for 16 licensed cores. It is particularly suited for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching systems, data analytics pipelines, and I/O-heavy indexing tasks where RAM and disk speed take precedence over raw parallel core count.
description: Microsoft Azure F16-4amds_v7 is a memory-dense, constrained-vCPU virtual machine designed for workloads requiring substantial RAM and local storage without high core counts. Powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, it offers 4 dedicated physical cores across 4 vCPUs, supported by 128.0 GB of memory and an integrated 1888 GB NVMe SSD. It features modern x86_64 execution flags including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, with no discrete GPU attached. Benchmark testing reveals top-tier single-core stress-ng throughput and strong lightweight LLM text generation rates, while multi-core compute metrics reflect the conservative 4-thread envelope. The high 32.0 GB per vCPU ratio makes the instance cost-effective for enterprise workloads subject to per-core software licensing fees, such as relational databases, in-memory caching layers, search indexes, and large-scale ETL jobs.
